WEEKS.title: Setup
WEEKS.intent: Two or three hours. Half the frustration in month one is environment problems, not concept problems.
build: Sign up for the Power Apps Developer Plan — free, full Dataverse sandbox for all 24 weeks
Create DEV, TEST and PROD environments if your tenant allows it
Sign in to Microsoft Learn so module progress tracks
Set up a notes repo — OneNote, Obsidian or GitHub
Run sample-data/generate.py — you build on invented people, not real personnel records
Book PL-900 for Week 5
WEEKS.ai: Nothing yet. Get the environments standing up first.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Environments live, PL-900 booked, sample data generated.
WEEKS.note: Do not start the Copilot Studio or Power Pages trials yet. They are timed — Week 17 and Week 20.

WEEKS.title: Platform orientation & environments
WEEKS.intent: Turn 'track training compliance' into a written brief with real entities and a real definition of compliant.
learn: PL-900 paths: business value and core components
Skim the PL-900T00-A course outline as your four-week roadmap
watch: April Dunnam — Power Platform overview (2026 content only)
Microsoft Power Platform official channel — current platform tour
build: Create your DEV environment; note its type, region and Dataverse status
Explore the Maker Portal, Admin Center and platform analytics
Write down the credentials your org actually requires, and which roles need each one
Define 'compliant' precisely — is someone expiring in 10 days compliant, or not?
WEEKS.ai: Have an AI assistant play requirements analyst and interrogate your definition of compliance: grace periods, provisional status, exemptions, people holding two roles. Those edge cases are the whole design.
WEEKS.checkpoint: One-page brief: the credentials, the roles that need them, and a precise definition of compliant.

WEEKS.title: Dataverse: tables, columns, relationships
WEEKS.intent: Six tables, one join. Simple enough to learn Dataverse rather than fight your own schema.
learn: Get started with Microsoft Dataverse
Create tables in Dataverse
watch: Shane Young — Dataverse table basics
Lisa Crosbie — Dataverse for beginners
build: Model on paper first: Person, Role, Credential, Role Requirement, Completion, Training Provider
Build the tables — Completion is the important one (person + credential + completed date + expiry date)
Role Requirement joins Role to Credential and is where 'who needs what' lives
Create the relationships; set cascade on delete so removing a Credential doesn't orphan Completions
Import the six CSVs from sample-data in numbered order, then spot-check that the superseded duplicates imported
WEEKS.ai: Ask AI to critique the schema as a Dataverse model — specifically whether Role Requirement should be a table or an N:N relationship, and what you lose either way. Then have it generate 40 rows of completions with realistic date spread.
WEEKS.checkpoint: An ERD you drew, plus six tables with completions that expire at staggered, believable dates.

WEEKS.title: Dataverse logic: keys, business rules, rollups
WEEKS.intent: Expiry dates are the engine of this whole solution. Get the calculation layer right before anything reads from it.
learn: Dataverse business logic: business rules, calculated columns, rollup columns, alternate keys
watch: Search: Dataverse business rules
Search: Dataverse rollup columns — Shane Young, Andrew Hess
build: Calculated column on Completion: days until expiry
Calculated column: status — Current, Expiring Soon, Lapsed — driven by that date
Rollup on Person: count of lapsed credentials (and meet the 12-hour recalculation lag the easy way)
Business rules: require Evidence when status is set to Completed; hide renewal fields on new records
Views: Expiring in 30 Days, Lapsed, Compliant, and My Team's Gaps
Alternate key on Completion (person + credential + completed date) for safe imports
WEEKS.ai: Ask whether 'days until expiry' should be a calculated column, a rollup, or a flow that stamps a value nightly — and what breaks with each at 10,000 rows. Verify against docs; this is exactly where AI overreaches.
WEEKS.checkpoint: A 300-word explainer on why you put expiry logic where you put it. The rollup lag should feature.

WEEKS.title: Security model
WEEKS.intent: Three roles with genuinely different reach. This is the design Week 18's portal will depend on.
learn: Dataverse security: business units, roles, teams, column-level security, hierarchy security, sharing
watch: Search: Dataverse security roles explained (2025–2026 only — business unit behaviour changed)
build: Create three roles: Staff, Manager, Compliance Officer
Staff read their own Completions only — privilege depth User
Manager reads their reports' Completions — depth Business Unit or Parent-Child
Compliance Officer reads and writes everything — depth Organization
Column-level security on any sensitive field (medical clearance, disciplinary notes)
Create a second user account, log in as them, and confirm Staff genuinely cannot see a colleague's record
WEEKS.ai: Have AI quiz you on PL-900 objectives — 25 scenario questions cold, then explanations for every miss, then five harder ones on your weakest domain.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Security matrix (role × table × privilege), verified by logging in as a Staff user and failing to see someone else's training.

WEEKS.title: PL-900 exam week
WEEKS.intent: Sit the exam. Then map the rest of the plan against the AB-410 objectives.
learn: Official PL-900 practice assessment on the Microsoft Learn credential page
Read the AB-410 study guide end to end — to map, not to study
build: Light review Monday to Wednesday
Sit PL-900 Thursday or Friday
Annotate every AB-410 objective with the week that covers it
WEEKS.ai: Ask AI to turn the AB-410 study guide into a checklist of discrete, testable skills. That checklist is your Week 16 self-assessment.
WEEKS.checkpoint: PL-900 passed. Annotated AB-410 objective map.

WEEKS.title: Model-driven apps
WEEKS.intent: The compliance officer's back office. Model-driven first, so you work with the data model rather than around it.
learn: Create a model-driven app with Dataverse
Optional: PL-7003 Applied Skill — model-driven apps
watch: Lisa Crosbie — model-driven app series (strong on the why, not just the click path)
build: Model-driven app for the compliance officer
Person main form with tabs: Details, Required Credentials, Completions, Gaps
Sub-grid on Person showing every Completion with expiry and status
Quick create for logging a completion in a hurry
Sitemap: People, Completions, Credentials, Roles, Providers
Chart: completions by status, and a view of everything lapsing in 60 days
WEEKS.ai: Ask AI to review the Person form for a compliance officer doing 30 record reviews an hour — field grouping, tab order, what should be visible without scrolling.
WEEKS.checkpoint: A compliance officer could open any person and answer 'are they current?' in under five seconds.

WEEKS.title: Business process flows
WEEKS.intent: A completion has a lifecycle: it gets scheduled, attended, evidenced, verified. Model it properly.
learn: Business process flows, form-level business rules, embedded canvas apps
watch: Search: business process flows Power Platform — cover the maker experience and the tables BPFs create
build: BPF on Completion: Required → Scheduled → Attended → Evidence Submitted → Verified
Stage-gate it — cannot reach Verified without an evidence attachment and a verifier
Business rules that show the provider and cost fields only from Scheduled onward
Embed a canvas app on the Person form showing a compliance summary
Editable grid on the Completions sub-grid for fast bulk date entry
WEEKS.ai: Ask AI to explain the table a BPF generates in Dataverse and why it matters when you later report on how long verification takes. Verify against docs.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Working BPF where a completion cannot be marked Verified without evidence attached.

WEEKS.title: Canvas apps & Power Fx
WEEKS.intent: The staff-facing app: what am I required to hold, what's expiring, what do I do about it.
learn: Create a canvas app in Power Apps
Power Fx formula reference
Optional: PL-7001 Applied Skill — canvas apps
watch: Reza Dorrani — canvas fundamentals and Power Fx
Shane Young — same ground, slower pace
build: Canvas app 'My Training' filtered to the signed-in user
Gallery of my credentials sorted by expiry, colour-coded by status — delegable filters only
A required-but-missing list, computed from my Role's Role Requirements
Form to request a renewal, using Patch with validation and error handling
Screens: My Training, Details, Request Renewal, Team View (managers only)
WEEKS.ai: Feed your filter formulas to AI for delegation review — date comparisons against Dataverse are where delegation quietly breaks. Verify every suggestion; models invent Power Fx functions that don't exist.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Zero delegation warnings, tested against 2,000+ completion rows.

WEEKS.title: Responsive design, components, performance
WEEKS.intent: The mobile case is real here: people finish external training and hold a paper certificate.
learn: Canvas components, responsive layouts, performance optimisation
watch: Reza Dorrani — responsive design and reusable components
Search: Power Apps performance optimization
build: Rebuild responsive with containers — managers will open this on a phone
Camera: photograph a paper certificate and attach it as evidence to a Completion
Barcode or QR scanner: scan a badge ID to check someone in at a training session
Two reusable components — a status pill and an expiry countdown chip
Optimise: concurrent loading, minimal OnStart, App.StartScreen so managers land on Team View
WEEKS.ai: Have AI generate a Power Fx theme object — status colours for Current, Expiring, Lapsed — and apply it globally so the app and the components agree.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Loads in under 3 seconds, and you have photographed a certificate onto a record from your actual phone.

WEEKS.title: Connectors & integration
WEEKS.intent: Connection references matter now because Week 24's ALM work depends on them.
learn: Connectors and data sources
Introduction to custom connectors
watch: Search: Power Apps custom connector — Reza Dorrani, Damien Bird
build: Office 365 Users connector to resolve a person's manager for escalation
Pull the signed-in user's profile so 'My Training' needs no manual identity mapping
Build one custom connector against a public REST API to learn the mechanics
Understand connection references properly
Write down your answer to: should Person be a Dataverse table, or the built-in Contact table?
WEEKS.ai: Give AI an OpenAPI spec, have it explain each operation and draft the connector definition. Import and test it.
WEEKS.checkpoint: The app resolves the signed-in user and their manager without a hardcoded lookup table.

WEEKS.title: Real users
WEEKS.intent: No new material. This is the week a study project becomes a work project.
build: Put 'My Training' in front of two or three colleagues — they don't need to know the domain
Watch them use it without helping — do not explain, do not defend
Ask one question only: 'is this list right?' Wrong data destroys trust faster than bad UI
Open Kwame's record (zero completions) in front of them — empty states are where apps look broken
Fix the top five problems they hit
Write a short user guide
WEEKS.ai: Feed your observation notes to AI and ask it to sort issues into UX, data model and training problems. The sorting is the point — each needs a different fix.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Three real people have used it. Bug list written, top five fixed.
WEEKS.note: Slack week. If you're behind, this is where you catch up.

WEEKS.title: Cloud flows: triggers, actions, expressions
WEEKS.intent: Date arithmetic is the core skill of this project and this week is where you learn it properly.
learn: Create flows in Power Automate
Optional: PL-7002 Applied Skill — automated processes
watch: Damien Bird and Reza Dorrani — both exceptional here
Search: Power Automate triggers explained / expressions
build: Scheduled flow: nightly scan of Completions for anything crossing 90, 60 or 30 days out
Automated flow on Completion create/update using filtering attributes so it fires only when expiry changes
Trigger condition preventing the flow re-triggering itself when it stamps a reminder-sent field
Instant flow from the canvas app to submit a renewal request
Master: formatDateTime, addDays, startOfDay, if, coalesce, first, length
Weekly digest flow listing everyone expiring in the next 30 days
WEEKS.ai: Describe each date calculation in plain English and get the expression. Strong AI use case — but test every one against a record you know the answer for, especially timezone handling.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Reminders fire at 90, 60 and 30 days with no duplicates and no self-triggering loop.

WEEKS.title: Approvals & error handling
WEEKS.intent: Evidence verification is an approval. Overdue credentials are an escalation. Both must fail loudly.
learn: Approvals, error handling patterns, scope and run-after configuration
watch: Search: Power Automate error handling try catch
Search: Power Automate approvals advanced
build: Approval flow: staff submits evidence, compliance officer approves or rejects with a reason
Rejection writes the reason back to the record and notifies the person
Escalation: lapsed for 7 days notifies the manager; 14 days notifies the manager's manager
Try / Catch / Finally using Scopes with configured run-after
Adaptive card approval posted to Teams so nobody has to open an app
Terminate with a meaningful message when a person has no manager set
WEEKS.ai: Ask AI to design a resilience strategy for the nightly expiry scan: what retries, what fails loudly, what degrades gracefully. A silent failure here means nobody gets warned — the worst outcome in the whole solution.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Break the nightly scan deliberately and confirm a human finds out it broke.

WEEKS.title: Child flows, HTTP, desktop flows
WEEKS.intent: Legacy systems are the norm in compliance. Your predecessor's spreadsheet is the point.
learn: Child flows, solution-aware flows, Power Automate Desktop basics
watch: Damien Bird — child flows and reusable patterns
Search: Power Automate Desktop tutorial 2026
build: Child flow that formats and sends a notification, called from the reminder, escalation and approval flows
Direct Dataverse Web API calls via HTTP with Azure AD auth
Desktop flow that opens the existing training spreadsheet or LMS export and loads completions into Dataverse
Apply to each with concurrency tuning on the nightly scan — and know when concurrency breaks your logic
WEEKS.ai: Ask AI to review your flow architecture for coupling: if you rename the expiry column, which flows break? Refactor the worst offender.
WEEKS.checkpoint: One child flow serving three parents, and a desktop flow that imports the old spreadsheet.

WEEKS.title: Business logic architecture
WEEKS.intent: You now have expiry logic in three or four different layers. Decide where it actually belongs.
learn: Dataverse plug-ins (conceptual), real-time vs background workflows, the full decision framework
watch: Search: Dataverse plugins vs flows — you want the architectural decision, not the C#
build: Document a decision tree: status calculation, reminder timing, compliance percentage, escalation — which layer and why
Refactor two pieces you put in the wrong place back in Phase 1
Settle the big one in writing: is status a calculated column read live, or a value a nightly flow stamps?
WEEKS.ai: Present the status-calculation question and ask for recommendations with tradeoffs — latency, reporting, licensing, what happens at 100,000 rows. Argue back where you disagree. The disagreement is the exercise.
WEEKS.checkpoint: A written business logic decision matrix for this solution. Genuinely SME-level output.

WEEKS.title: Buffer & consolidation
WEEKS.intent: Deliberate slack. If you're on schedule, bank credentials. If you're behind, you're now caught up.
build: Rebuild your weakest Phase 2 component with what you know now
Sit the free PL-7001, PL-7002 and PL-7003 Applied Skills assessments
Score yourself 1–5 against every AB-410 objective
WEEKS.ai: Have AI generate a 40-question mixed practice set from the AB-410 study guide, weighted toward your low scores.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Honest self-assessment against every AB-410 objective.

WEEKS.title: Power Pages foundations
WEEKS.intent: Staff need to see and act on their own record without a Power Apps licence. That's what Pages is for.
WEEKS.trial: Start your Power Pages trial now (30 days, renewable).
learn: Get started with Power Pages
Demonstrate the capabilities of Microsoft Power Pages
watch: Dhruvin Shah — the most complete Power Pages content on YouTube
Search: Power Pages tutorial 2026
build: Provision a site from a template
Design Studio: pages, sections, navigation, styling, theming
A My Credentials page listing the signed-in person's completions with expiry dates
A form to upload a certificate as evidence
Publish, then view it signed out and confirm nothing leaks
WEEKS.ai: Ask AI to draft the information architecture: what someone sees on landing, how they learn they're lapsed, and how few clicks it takes to fix it.
WEEKS.checkpoint: A published site showing a real person their real credentials.

WEEKS.title: Portal security & table permissions
WEEKS.intent: This is the week that matters, and this project is the ideal case for it: everyone sees their own record and nobody else's.
learn: Work with Power Pages websites — authentication, table permissions, web roles
build: Configure authentication plus at least one external identity provider
Table permission with Self scope so a person reads only their own Completions
Table permission with Contact or Account scope so a manager reads their team's
Web roles: Staff, Manager, Compliance Officer — mirroring your Week 4 Dataverse roles
Multistep form for evidence submission with save-and-resume
Sign in as one person, take another person's record GUID, put it in the URL, and confirm you get nothing
WEEKS.ai: Describe your table permission config and ask AI to find data exposure risks — then verify each manually. Don't outsource the conclusion; a confident wrong answer here exposes staff records.
WEEKS.checkpoint: A written security test log: 8+ access scenarios, expected result, actual result. The URL-tampering test must fail closed.

WEEKS.title: Liquid, Web API, custom code
WEEKS.intent: Turn the portal from a content site into something people actually transact on.
learn: Extend Power Pages — Liquid, Web API, ALM
watch: Dhruvin Shah — Liquid templates and Portal Web API in depth
build: Liquid rendering the signed-in person's completions — fetchxml, entitylist, entityview
A team compliance summary page for managers, rendered with Liquid
Portal Web API for client-side evidence upload without a full page reload
Custom JavaScript validating that a completion date isn't in the future
Portal submission triggers your Week 13 approval flow
Custom CSS matched to your organisation's brand
WEEKS.ai: Have AI generate the Liquid, then explain the security implications of every tag used. Liquid will happily render records the user shouldn't see if your permissions are loose.
WEEKS.checkpoint: A person uploads a certificate on the portal, it writes to Dataverse, the approval fires, the compliance officer is notified.

WEEKS.title: Copilot Studio foundations
WEEKS.intent: The questions people ask about compliance are repetitive and predictable. That is exactly what an agent is for.
WEEKS.trial: Start your Copilot Studio trial now (60 days).
learn: Copilot Studio fundamentals: agents, topics, knowledge sources, actions
AI Builder and AI Hub: prompts, models, prebuilt models — AB-410 objectives
watch: Nick DeCourcy (Bright Ideas Agency) — Copilot Studio depth
Daniel Christian — focused agent tutorials
Lisa Crosbie — Copilot inside apps
build: Agent with topics for: am I current, what am I missing, when does X expire, how do I renew
Knowledge sources: your training policy document, the provider list, a renewal FAQ
Action calling a flow that looks up the asker's own completions
Action that files a renewal request on their behalf
Generative answers scoped so it refuses to discuss anyone else's records
Publish to Teams and test with a real colleague
WEEKS.ai: Iterate the agent's instructions with AI: draft, test against ten real questions, feed the failures back, revise. Pay attention to it answering about other people — that's the failure that matters.
WEEKS.checkpoint: A published agent that tells you your own status and refuses to tell you someone else's.

WEEKS.title: AB-410 exam week
WEEKS.intent: Broad exam. Expect scenario clusters and more weight on BPFs and business rules than you'd guess.
learn: AB-410 study guide, three domains — target your lowest Week 16 scores
build: Focused review Monday to Wednesday
Sit AB-410 Thursday or Friday
WEEKS.ai: Have AI drill you on scenario questions in the exam's style — multi-part, linked to a single business situation, rather than isolated facts.
WEEKS.checkpoint: AB-410 passed.
WEEKS.note: Microsoft Learn is available inside the exam. Safety net, not a strategy. Retakes allowed after 24 hours, but use the score report to rebuild first.

WEEKS.title: MCP, multi-agent, Foundry
WEEKS.intent: AB-620 territory and the genuine frontier of the platform.
learn: AB-620 study guide: plan and configure, integrate and extend, test and manage
build: Connect your agent to an MCP server as a tool source
Build a second specialist agent — a Training Finder that searches provider catalogues — and hand off to it
Custom connectors and API actions as agent tools
Adaptive cards rendering a person's credential list with expiry chips
A custom prompt from the Microsoft Foundry model catalog
Explore computer use for a UI-driven task, such as booking on a provider's website
WEEKS.ai: Use AI to design the decomposition — the compliance agent knows records, the finder agent knows courses, and neither should do the other's job. Reasoning about boundaries out loud is how you get good at this.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Two agents, one MCP tool integration, one working handoff from compliance to training-finder.

WEEKS.title: Agent evaluation & testing
WEEKS.intent: Almost nobody does this part. That is exactly why it differentiates you.
learn: AB-620 domain three: test sets, evaluation methods, Application Insights, solutions and pipelines
build: A test set of 30+ real questions staff would ask, with expected outcomes
Run evaluations, review results, iterate on instructions and knowledge
Wire up Application Insights for agent telemetry
Package the agent into a solution with environment variables — no hardcoded values
Deploy DEV to TEST via Power Platform Pipelines
WEEKS.ai: Ask AI for 40 adversarial utterances, weighted toward attempts to extract another person's training records by indirect phrasing. That is the specific risk in this solution, and it's real red-teaming.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Evaluation results before and after one iteration, showing measured improvement — and zero cross-user leaks.

WEEKS.title: ALM, governance & the rebuild
WEEKS.intent: The capstone. Package it properly, ship it through a pipeline, and write down why you built it the way you did.
learn: ALM for Power Platform, solutions, Power Platform Pipelines
CoE Starter Kit, DLP policies, environment strategy
watch: Search: Power Platform ALM pipelines 2026
Search: Power Platform CoE Starter Kit
build: Package everything as a managed solution with proper publisher and prefix
Externalise every connection reference and environment variable — reminder thresholds should not be hardcoded
Full DEV to TEST to PROD deployment via pipelines
Apply a DLP policy and document its impact — this solution handles staff records
Install the CoE Starter Kit in a sandbox and explore what it surfaces
Write an architecture decision record: the status-calculation choice, the security model, the portal permission design
Sit AB-620 this week or next, depending on how Weeks 22–23 went
WEEKS.ai: Have AI argue the opposing side of every decision in your ADR. Where you can't defend yourself, you've found a gap.
WEEKS.checkpoint: Deployed to PROD through a pipeline. ADR written. Real staff checking their own compliance.
